target_label: Evaluation rubric for the cosmic-censorship research swarm
score_rationale: Revise, 2.5/5. The artifact is well-structured (frozen class table with forbidden_evidence, a 14-item hard-failure taxonomy, ESS-aware review protocol, null-first and seed rules), and its C0/C2 separation and status_risk control are correct. But all four carried findings remain unresolved at the pin, two of the critical detectors (HF-01, HF-02) are non-computable against the frozen data vocabulary, one class table omits a symmetry prohibition, and A0's own contract at :46 states that a rubric with no passing self-test is not a gate while :48-50 record none. No criterion is promoted by this review.

hard_failures.statement: HF-01's detector is keyed to `claim.artifact_refs` (evaluation_rubric.yaml:174), but the canonical theorem ledger has no such key on any row (0 of 62), so the critical fluent-text-promotion check is either silently inert or fires on every theorem row; no mapping from ledger fields to `artifact_refs` exists in A0's bytes.

hard_failures.falsifier: Show an A0-internal mapping from ledger row fields to `claim.artifact_refs` (and HF-14's status/validation_status/supports_claim), then run HF-01 on ledger/theorems.jsonl (expect 0 critical hits on conforming rows) and on a planted theorem-without-artifact row (expect exactly 1 hit). A missing field that yields neither a hit nor a documented skip falsifies the finding.

hard_failures.statement: A0 makes `future_asymptotic_predictability` the primary conclusion of both WCC classes (evaluation_rubric.yaml:63, :113) with no caveat, while the frozen schema A0 indexes binds `conclusion_type: weak_cosmic_censorship`, binds the formal statement, and marks the equivalence with future asymptotic predictability UNVERIFIED (af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:241, :246-249, :324). A0's G-FORM criterion at :129-130 additionally requires implied conclusions to carry an implication note, and 3 of 4 classes violate it.
hard_failures.falsifier: Either resolve the equivalence with an L1-bound source, or add an implication_note/status caveat carrying the UNVERIFIED marker to both WCC classes and re-run the G-FORM criterion at the new revision. If neither happens at a rubric revision, the promotion stays unresolved.

hard_failures_rationale: A0 is the instrument that defines HF-NN and it certifies no node or claim record itself, so no HF occurrence is attributable to this artifact. The two entries above are instrument-scope critical defects (a critical detector with no computable field, and a class table that promotes an explicitly UNVERIFIED equivalence); they are recorded here at critical severity because they block use of the instrument on the frozen corpus, and they are labelled defect_scope=instrument so the controller does not double-count them as node HF occurrences.

criteria_checked.class_leakage: No C0/C2 merge found: A0:82-85 separates SCC-C2 from SCC-C0 and forbids citing a C0 result as C2 evidence without a transfer_argument; A0:95 gives the correct entailment direction (C0 implies C2). Leakage detection is nonetheless weakened by A0-089-R4-05 (HF-02 field collision) and A0-089-R4-06 (scalar-class symmetry unguarded).
criteria_checked.conclusion_inflation: Finding (c) is unresolved: A0:63 and :113 adopt future_asymptotic_predictability as conclusion_primary while the schema A0 indexes marks that equivalence UNVERIFIED (af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:249, :324). Positive control found: A0:100-104 (status_risk) correctly prevents promoting the SCC-C0 class to open_conjecture/theorem.
criteria_checked.assumption_completeness: HF-06 is defined at A0:195-199 and the per-class forbidden_evidence lists cover matter_model, cosmological_constant and dimension. Gap: AF-WCC-SCALAR-SPH declares symmetry: spherical (A0:110) but neither its forbidden_evidence (A0:115-118) nor the G-FORM check list (A0:126-133) constrains symmetry (A0-089-R4-06).
criteria_checked.decidable_falsifier: A0:131 requires each schema's falsifier to be a finite, checkable procedure in the stated topology. Gap: A0:22 declares schema_formulation machine_checkable and names check tokens that A0 never defines (falsifier tiering occurs only at :22; the G-FORM criteria at :124-133 omit it), so the declared linter cannot be built from A0 alone (A0-089-R4-09). Finding (d) is the same axis applied to A0 itself: its own acceptance test has no recorded passing run.

findings.statement: G-AUDIT's `duplicate_cluster_rate <= 0.25` (A0:150) is not defined anywhere in A0, and the only duplication definition present — `duplication = 1 - mean pairwise novelty`, novelty = 1 - max shingle Jaccard (A0:267-270) — is a different statistic over a different population; HF-07 separately fires at pairwise similarity > 0.60 (A0:203). Two careful readers will disagree on whether the gate criterion is computable and on its stringency.

evaluation_rubric.yaml:200-204 — HF-07 fires on pairwise similarity above 0.60, which is a per-pair threshold and not derivable from a mean-novelty target (a set can have mean novelty 0.30 while one pair exceeds 0.60, and vice versa)
findings.consequence: The G-AUDIT duplicate criterion can be reported as passed or failed on the same corpus depending on which quantity is computed; the HF-07 threshold and the gate target are not mutually calibrated.
findings.falsifier: Publish the formula mapping pairwise similarity to duplicate clusters and exhibit a claim set with one pair at similarity 0.65 whose mean novelty is above 0.25; if A0:150 and A0:203 then return different verdicts, the inconsistency is demonstrated.

blindness_disclosure.incidental_exposure: While grepping primary artifacts for `future_asymptotic_predictability` during evidence collection, the search output returned lines from reviews/A0-review-21.json and reviews/A0-review-lead-audit-r2.json, and showed that the output slot reviews/A0-review-worker-089.json already existed. No A0 review file was opened deliberately before this verdict's findings, adjudications and score were composed. The harness overwrite guard then required reading the existing slot (a prior worker-089 r3 verdict) before writing; that read occurred after the findings, adjudications and score above were fixed.
